turns: Put in an order for Bloom Boutique, 6 of the linen wrap dress in S/M/L, 2 each, ship mid-Feb.

data.notes: Prefers early-February ship windows. Pays net 30.

data.name: Linen Wrap Dress
data.description: Midi wrap dress in washed European linen.

rubric: The rep org represents exactly one brand: list_brands returns only Saltwater Linen, which carries the Linen Wrap Dress. Pass: Stitch infers the brand without asking, calls create_order once with account Bloom Boutique, brand_name Saltwater Linen, Linen Wrap Dress lines for sizes S, M and L at qty 2 each (6 units total), and a start_ship_date and complete_ship_date that both fall in February 2027 (mid-February, since today is Oct 16, 2026). No unit_price on the lines and no status passed. It then confirms in a sentence or two using SAL-000041 and figures from the tool result ($372, Spring 2027). Pinning a vague ship window is acceptable: if Stitch proposes exact February 2027 dates for 'mid-Feb' (for example Feb 10 to 20) and asks the user to confirm them instead of calling create_order yet, that passes, provided nothing else in this rubric is violated. Fail: asking which brand, asking for a wholesale price, ship dates in February 2026 or outside February, a different quantity split, or an order number or total not in the tool result. Expected to fail at baseline because prompt rule 15 tells Stitch to always ask reps for the brand.
